name: layerpath
description: Turn screenshots, screen recordings, Loom videos or YouTube links into interactive product walkthroughs you can edit, share and export as videos or PDF guides.

interface.longDescription:
Layerpath turns screenshots, screen recordings, Loom videos or YouTube links into interactive product walkthroughs with clickable steps and callouts over your real screens. Product, support, sales and training teams use them to explain software workflows. In Layerpath, a walkthrough is called a tour. Sign in with your Layerpath account or create one. Walkthroughs are saved to the workspace you select.

In the chat, you can:
- Create walkthroughs from attached screenshots, screen recordings, Loom videos or YouTube links.
- Find walkthroughs by name, open them and play them in the chat.
- Open a walkthrough in Layerpath's editor to change its steps by hand.
- Edit step text, rename walkthroughs, reorder, merge, hide or delete steps, and change intro and outro content.
- Change callout colors and styles, backgrounds and browser frames.
- Blur private information, including names and email addresses, in screenshots.
- Translate a walkthrough or duplicate it in another language.
- Add voiceover using an AI voice.
- Get share and embed links, or export a walkthrough as a video or a PDF guide.
- Undo a change made through the chat.

When Layerpath creates a walkthrough, it publishes it at a share link accessible to anyone with the link. Requesting a share link, or turning on Publish in Share, also publishes an unpublished walkthrough. Changes to published walkthroughs appear at their share links immediately. You can unpublish or delete walkthroughs in Layerpath. Repeating a creation, duplication or video export request creates another output each time.

Layerpath works with existing screens and walkthroughs in your connected workspace. It doesn't design new interfaces or create text-only documents.
defaultPrompt: Make an interactive walkthrough from these screenshots
Turn this Loom recording into a step-by-step walkthrough

positive.description: Make a tour from attached screenshots
positive.prompt: Make an interactive tour from these screenshots of inviting a teammate.
positive.expected_behavior: Layerpath starts the tour straight away (ChatGPT may ask to confirm first, since this makes a new tour). ChatGPT says Layerpath is making the tour. Layerpath's view in the chat shows the tour's progress. Within about 2 minutes it shows the finished tour about inviting a teammate, which plays in the chat: one step for each screenshot in the order attached, each with a callout. When it's ready, a short message in the chat says so and ChatGPT says what can be asked next. The tour has Edit, which opens it in Layerpath's editor (beside the chat on plans with the side panel), and Share, with the tour's link, embed code, video and PDF exports, and step-by-step guide. The tour is published at its share link. Each run makes a new tour.

positive.description: Find a tour by name and show it
positive.prompt: Show me my Connect a calendar tour.
positive.expected_behavior: Layerpath shows the Connect a calendar tour in the chat, where it plays: step through it or press play. It has Edit, which opens the tour in Layerpath's editor (beside the chat on plans with the side panel), and Share, with the tour's link, embed code, video and PDF exports, and step-by-step guide. ChatGPT answers in a sentence or two and doesn't list the steps. Nothing is published or changed.

positive.prompt: In my Create a report tour, make every callout shorter.
positive.expected_behavior: Layerpath reads the tour, then saves shorter words for every step (edit_tour in place of update_steps is also right). Every callout in Create a report is shorter than before and still names the same buttons and fields. ChatGPT says what changed, and opening the tour in Layerpath shows the new words.

positive.description: Translate a tour into a new copy
positive.prompt: Make a Spanish copy of my Set up billing tour.
positive.expected_behavior: Layerpath makes one new copy of the tour, and ChatGPT names the copy. ChatGPT may say the translation is still finishing; within about 2 minutes every callout in the copy is in Spanish. The Set up billing tour stays in English. If a Spanish copy from an earlier run is still in the workspace, ChatGPT may point to that copy instead of making another.

positive.prompt: Give me the share link for my Export contacts tour.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT may ask to confirm first, since sharing publishes a draft. It then replies with the tour's share link and embed link, sometimes as links named after the tour. If the tour was still a draft, it says the tour is now published. The share link opens the tour in a browser without signing in.

negative.description: The request is for a web page, not a tour of existing screens. Layerpath should not run. ChatGPT should create the HTML itself.
negative.prompt: Build me a landing page for my bakery in HTML with a hero section and a menu.

negative.description: The request is for a text-only SOP, which Layerpath doesn't create. ChatGPT should write the document without calling Layerpath tools.
negative.prompt: Write a one-page SOP for how our support team handles refund requests. Policy: refunds within 30 days, manager approval over $500, log every refund in Zendesk.

negative.description: The request is for a prototype without existing screens. Layerpath should not run. ChatGPT should help with the prototype using its own capabilities.
negative.prompt: Mock up a clickable prototype for a habit-tracker app idea. I don't have any designs yet.

review.commerce_description: Layerpath doesn't sell products or process purchases in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: First release of Layerpath in ChatGPT. Create interactive walkthroughs from screenshots, screen recordings, Loom videos or YouTube links. Find, open, play and edit walkthroughs, including their steps, callouts, appearance, intro and outro. Blur private information, translate walkthroughs, add AI voiceover, share or embed walkthroughs, and export videos and PDF guides. Sign in with your Layerpath account.
